text: Alright, let's start by setting up our workspace here in the engineering lab. First, the carbon fiber frame components were carefully laid out by Sarah on the clean workbench, along with the high-precision brushless motors that we ordered last week. Now, I'm going to put together the main quadcopter frame while Sarah heats up the soldering iron to exactly 350 degrees Fahrenheit. The experienced drone technician with over 8 years of UAV experience always recommends starting with the central hub piece that connects all four motor arms. Next, we need to hook up the electronic speed controllers, or ESCs, which were pre-programmed by our software team yesterday using the latest firmware. Sarah is now taking apart the protective packaging from the delicate flight control board that weighs precisely 28 grams. After that, I'll set up the GPS module on the top plate while measuring the exact center point with my digital calipers - we need it positioned within 2 millimeters of the geometric center. The battery connector that Sarah is installing requires a Torx T15 screwdriver bit from our professional toolkit. Before we turn on the power systems, the propeller balance weights were adjusted by me using a specialized balancing jig that cost 400 dollars. While I'm connecting the telemetry radio and Sarah is checking the motor timing, we also need to break in each motor for about 30 seconds at low throttle. Finally, the calibration sequence that we'll run takes approximately 3 minutes and tests all the sensors that the flight controller depends on for stable hover performance.
